Publication-quality prescribing time series

Source: R/plots.R
op_plot_trend.Rd

Draws one line per antimicrobial (or other group) with direct labels at the right-hand end instead of a legend. Output of op_spending(), op_spending_ab() or op_antibiotic_use() can be passed directly.

Usage

op_plot_trend(
  data,
  y = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  facet = NULL,
  date = "date",
  highlight = NULL,
  max_groups = 8L,
  label = TRUE,
  log = FALSE,
  zero = TRUE,
  events = NULL,
  facet_scales = c("free_y", "fixed"),
  ylab = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  source = TRUE,
  base_size = 8
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with a date column and a numeric column to plot.

y

Column to plot. Default "rate" if present, otherwise "items".

group

Column that defines the lines. If NULL (default) it is "ab_name" or "code" when present with more than one value, otherwise a single series is drawn.

facet

Optional column to split into small multiples (free y-axes by default). If facet is given and group is NULL, each panel shows one line in a single colour with no direct label (the panel title names the series).

date

Date column (default "date").

highlight

Groups to colour; all others are drawn in light grey without labels. If NULL and there are more than max_groups groups, the max_groups groups with the highest final value are highlighted.

max_groups

Maximum number of coloured groups when highlight is NULL (default 8, the size of the colour-blind safe palette).

label

Draw direct labels (default TRUE).

log

Use a log10 y-axis (default FALSE). Lines only; never bars.

zero

Start a linear y-axis at zero (default TRUE).

events

Optional data frame with columns date and label to mark events with a dashed vertical line and a label.

facet_scales

Scales for facets: "free_y" (default) or "fixed".

ylab, title, subtitle

Text. title should state the finding in a sentence; it is NULL by default (put the message in the figure caption of your paper).

source

Add the data-source caption (default TRUE); or a custom character string.

base_size

Base font size (default 8 pt, see theme_op()).

Value

A ggplot2::ggplot() object.

Examples

ex <- op_example[op_example$ab_name %in%
  c("Amoxicillin", "Doxycycline", "Nitrofurantoin", "Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid"), ]
op_plot_trend(ex, y = "items")

op_plot_trend(ex, y = "items", highlight = "Nitrofurantoin", log = TRUE)
